primitives.name: Three-Step Hurdle Method
primitives.verbatim_quote: The usual three-step method is pre ferred for the high hurdles, and the jump and stride should be a jump clearing close to fourteen feet, next step five feet, next six, next five again, then flight.
primitives.assumptions: Constant acceleration, idealized step timing, negligible air resistance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Stride deviation beyond ±0.5 ft leads to inefficient clearance.

layer2.mapping: Hurdle clearance trajectory modeled as piecewise linear kinematic segments with fixed angular momentum.

primitives.name: Hurdle Distance Adaptation
primitives.verbatim_quote: When learning this three-step the novice should place the hurdles sufficiently near together to enable him to get his stride, then he can increase the distance as his strength increases until he reaches the regulation ten yards.
primitives.assumptions: Linear scaling of stride length with hurdle spacing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Spacing exceeding 12 yards causes stride misalignment.

layer2.mapping: Adaptive stride optimization via iterative feedback loop between hurdle spacing and athlete performance metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Stride-to-hurdle ratio stability, cumulative fatigue index.

primitives.name: Pre-Race Hurdle Practice Regimen
primitives.verbatim_quote: In mid-season the hurdler should occasionally go over six or seven hurdles, and three weeks before the race, the full course.
primitives.assumptions: Practice intensity scales inversely with competition proximity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient practice within 3 weeks results in reduced race performance.

layer2.mapping: Training load distribution mapped to race readiness via temporal decay functions.
layer2.telemetry: Performance decline rate, practice volume vs. race outcome correlation.
